definition: A training approach that fine-tunes a model specifically to make better use of retrieved documents provided in its context, improving RAG system performance.
details: RAFT-style approaches train models to distinguish relevant from irrelevant retrieved passages and to cite evidence appropriately, addressing weaknesses that arise when a general-purpose model is simply given retrieved context at inference time without task-specific training.
story: Picture a potter shaping clay on a spinning wheel: every nudge is tiny, but each one is guided by how the last attempt wobbled. Here is the short version: A training approach that fine-tunes a model specifically to make better use of retrieved documents provided in its context, improving RAG system performance. The part that makes it sing: RAFT-style approaches train models to distinguish relevant from irrelevant retrieved passages and to cite evidence appropriately, addressing weaknesses that arise when a general-purpose model is simply given retrieved context at inference time without task-specific training. Each pass is a tiny course-correction — the model gets a little less wrong every time. And that is Retrieval-Augmented Fine-Tuning — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.
